label: Aquinas, ST I q.14 a.1: immateriality explains cognition and its degrees
locator: I q.14 a.1 co.: immaterialitas alicuius rei est ratio quod sit cognoscitiva
interpretation: The article relates cognitive ability and its degree to immateriality: plants are described as lacking cognition because of materiality; sense receives forms without matter; intellect is further removed from matter; God, already assumed highest in immateriality, is said to have the highest cognition. The passage does not define 'altogether immaterial' as both not matter–form composite and not a component of anything, or assert for every arbitrary bearer that those two negations guarantee intellect. Those are analyst criteria/bridge steps in STMT-IMMATERIAL-IS-INTELLECTUAL, now linked only by non-deductive support.
attribution: The passage states that immateriality accounts for cognitive capacity and the degree of knowing, and concludes that God, as maximally immaterial, has the highest cognition, which is the premise.
